case_title: Harilal etc. v. State of Madhya Pradesh (now Chhattisgarh)
weapon: Lathi (wooden stick); PW-6 earlier described the weapon as danda (stick)
evidence_type: Eyewitness (ocular), medical (autopsy), recovery (lathi and clothes seizures)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC s.302 and sentenced to life imprisonment (Sessions Judge, Bilaspur, 13.07.1991)
high_court_outcome: Appeals dismissed; conviction and life sentence affirmed (judgment dated 17.02.2010)
neutral_facts: In the late evening of the incident, the victim was allegedly assaulted with lathis in an open street in front of a house in a village, by several men identified as the accused. Two eyewitnesses said they saw the assault. One of them had earlier given a police statement that differed from his court testimony, and the other was not present when the assault began and said he came out after an alarm that the victim was beating the son of one of the accused. Neither eyewitness lodged a report. A named first information report was lodged the next morning at about 10 am by a village chowkidar of a neighbouring village, who said no eyewitness had informed her; she had come to the spot after hearing loud noises and found the body near a temple. Villagers guarded the body overnight. The next day, the police conducted an inquest, collected blood-stained earth from the spot, and seized a lathi lying near the body. The site plan showed that the body was about 300 feet from the place of assault, and drag marks were noticed. Lathis and clothes were said to have been recovered at the instance of each accused from their houses, but the serologist could not confirm the origin of the blood on them. The autopsy recorded lacerations to the left temple and left ear, contusions on the left thigh, rib fractures on both sides, lung contusions, and extradural haemorrhage in the left temporal region. Death was attributed to shock from brain and lung injuries, with time since death of 24 to 48 hours.
physical_harm: Death of the victim; lacerated wounds to left temporal region and left ear, three thigh contusions, rib fractures on both sides, lung contusions, extradural haemorrhage
premeditation_planning: Not found. The court found a strong probability of a spontaneous mob action; no planning was discussed.
motive: alleged: victim's involvement with a lady of the village (court held no clear motive proved)
key_evidence_accepted: None relied on to convict. The court found the eyewitness evidence unsafe and the lathi and clothes seizure not clinching; the court relied on the delayed FIR, the body location and the gaps in the story to hold the case unproven.
witness_credibility: PW-2 (eyewitness): unsafe to rely on; chance witness, inconsistent with prior statement, did not name all accused. PW-6 (eyewitness): not of stellar quality; chance witness, inconsistent with prior statement, conduct did not inspire confidence. PW-9 (informant chowkidar): her testimony that no eyewitness informed her was given significant weight.
post_offence_conduct: Alleged by prosecution: recovery of lathis and clothes from the accused's houses. Court did not treat these as clinching; no other post-offence conduct found.
custody_duration: Not stated (defence submission only that the appellants had served over 10 years during trial and appeal; the court recorded no finding)
bail_history: Released on bail during pendency of the Supreme Court appeal
trial_duration: offence: 25.08.1989; trial judgment: 13.07.1991; High Court: 17.02.2010; Supreme Court: 05.09.2023
legal_representation: Appellants: D. N. Goburdhun, Sr. Adv., with Aakarsh Kamra and Ms. Gauri Goburdhun. State: Mrs. Prachi Mishra, AAG, with others.
investigation_status: FIR registered 26.08.1989 at P.S. Hirri; inquest, seizures, site plan and autopsy conducted; third accused arrested 27.08.1989; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Trial court and High Court did not properly address material aspects and did not carefully consider the deposition of PW-9; FIR was delayed without proper explanation.
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.302 IPC, life imprisonment. High Court: appeals dismissed, conviction affirmed. Supreme Court: appeals allowed, accused acquitted.
prosecution_argument: FIR not delayed or contrived since the body was guarded overnight; PW-2 a natural witness; PW-6 consistent with medical evidence; lathi and clothes recovery corroborated by serologist; injuries showed merciless beating; no Exception under s.300 pleaded, so s.302 conviction proper.
defence_argument: Delayed FIR suggests no witness and a developed story; PW-2 and PW-6 unreliable due to inconsistencies and conduct. Alternatively, a street fight over a lady warranted conviction under s.304 Part I IPC.
legal_principle_applied: Delayed FIR without explanation requires meticulous testing of evidence; chance-witness and prior-inconsistency analysis; accused entitled to benefit of doubt where genesis, manner and perpetrators are not convincingly proved.
other_sentence_order: Bail bonds discharged; no surrender required; release forthwith if not on bail unless wanted in another case
